History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
34-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and mild hypertension presents with a 5-day history of dry cough, rhinorrhea, myalgias, chills, and mild sore throat—clinical picture most consistent with an uncomplicated viral upper respiratory tract infection; advised symptomatic care and red-flag follow-up.

History:
• Presenting complaint: “Cough and cold.”  
• Onset & duration: Began ~5 days ago (start of last weekend).  
• Character: Dry, hacking cough; associated runny nose.  
• Associated symptoms: Generalized muscle aches, occasional headache, chills; mild throat discomfort.  
• Negatives: No sputum production, no hemoptysis, no shortness of breath, no wheeze, no chest pain, no palpable neck glands.  
• Home monitoring: Reports normal capillary blood glucose readings; morning home BP “within the normal range” (values not provided).  
• Self-care to date: Paracetamol for symptom relief; no ibuprofen; has not used OTC cold combinations yet.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: None specified.  
• Review of other systems: Not discussed.

Past Medical History:
• Type 2 diabetes mellitus – diagnosed ~5–6 years ago; self-monitoring glucose, no current complications reported.  
• Mild hypertension – controlled on lisinopril.  
• No other chronic conditions stated.

Medications:
• Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Lisinopril – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Paracetamol as needed for current symptoms – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
Allergies: Not documented.

Social History:
• Secure environment confirmed for tele-consult.  
• Smoking, alcohol, illicit substance use, occupation, and living situation: Not documented.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: Not recorded.  
• HEENT: Mild pharyngeal erythema; tonsils not enlarged; no cervical lymphadenopathy.  
• Respiratory: Chest not examined during video session; patient denies wheeze or shortness of breath.  
• Cardiovascular, abdominal, neurologic, skin: Not recorded.

Investigations:
• None performed or ordered at this visit.

Assessment & Plan:
Overall Impression:
Acute viral upper respiratory tract infection (common cold) in a patient with well-controlled type 2 diabetes and hypertension.

DDx Integration (aligned with transcript):
1. Viral upper respiratory tract infection – acute onset, rhinorrhea, dry cough, myalgias; benign throat findings.  
2. Influenza-like illness – systemic aches/chills support; less likely given mild course and no fever.  
3. ACE-inhibitor-related cough – possible due to lisinopril but unlikely because of concomitant coryzal symptoms and abrupt onset.

Issue 1: Upper respiratory tract infection (viral)
• Assessment: Uncomplicated common cold; no red-flag features.  
• Plan:  
  – OTC combination therapy (e.g., Day Nurse/Night Nurse) acceptable with current meds.  
  – Continue paracetamol as needed.  
  – Hydration, rest, symptomatic care.  
  – Red-flag advice: seek care if shortness of breath, wheeze, worsening severity, or symptoms persist >3 weeks.  
  – No antibiotics or additional prescriptions needed today.

Issue 2: Type 2 diabetes mellitus – stable
• Plan: Continue metformin; continue home glucose monitoring. Advise maintaining usual diet and hydration; seek medical review if hyperglycemia develops during illness.

Issue 3: Hypertension – stable
• Plan: Continue lisinopril; continue home BP monitoring; report sustained elevations or symptoms.

General plan items:
• Safety-net instructions provided verbally.  
• Follow-up: Virtual or in-person review if red-flag symptoms develop or no improvement by 3 weeks.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: Allergies, full medication doses, vitals, smoking/alcohol status, family history.  
● No conflicts between transcript and DDx identified.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; limited physical exam inherent to video format.
